name: Greece
description:
Cradle of Western civilization, Greece offers ancient history, Mediterranean charm, and island living. With affordable costs, excellent cuisine, and a relaxed lifestyle, Greece attracts expats from around the world.

## Key Highlights
- Cradle of Western civilization with ancient history
- Affordable cost of living with Mediterranean lifestyle
- Beautiful islands and world-class cuisine
longdescription: Greece is a Mediterranean nation with profound historical significance as the birthplace of Western democracy, philosophy, and classical civilization. Athens, the capital, is home to the Parthenon and thousands of ancient ruins that shaped Western thought. The country consists of mainland territories and numerous islands, each with distinct character and beauty. Greek islands like Santorini, Mykonos, and Crete are world-famous vacation destinations with white-washed buildings, blue domes, and Mediterranean culture. The cost of living is affordable compared to Northern Europe, particularly outside major tourist areas and Athens. Greek cuisine is Mediterranean excellence: fresh seafood, olives, feta cheese, and healthy cooking traditions. Wine production is ancient, with many regions producing excellent local varieties. The Greek lifestyle emphasizes community, family, and enjoying life's pleasures. Healthcare is adequate and affordable. Greek is the official language; English proficiency varies. The economy has recovered from previous crises but remains moderately developed. Greece offers various residency programs for entrepreneurs, investors, and remote workers. Expats are attracted by affordability, Mediterranean beauty, island living, history, and relaxed lifestyle. Challenges include bureaucratic complexity, sometimes inconsistent services, and economic uncertainty. Greece combines ancient history, Mediterranean beauty, affordable living, excellent cuisine, island lifestyle, and cultural richness, making it attractive for retirees, digital nomads, and those seeking Mediterranean living with historical depth.

visas.name: Greece Digital Nomad Visa
visas.description: Greece's visa for remote workers who want to live and work from the beautiful Greek islands or mainland.

visas.name: Residence by investment (Greece)
visas.description: Residence by investment program for real estate purchases in Greece, offering EU residency.

visas.name: Greece Student Visa (Type D)
visas.description: Greece's student visa (Type D) for non-EU/EEA nationals enrolled in a full-time study programme at a Greek university or accredited institution for more than 90 days.

visas.name: Greece Family Reunification Permit
visas.description: Greece's family reunification permit allows non-EU spouses and minor dependent children of non-EU residents legally living in Greece for at least two years to join them.

visas.name: Greece Self-Employment Visa
visas.description: Greece's self-employment visa allows non-EU nationals to establish and run their own business or work as an independent professional in Greece, subject to proof of business viability and financial stability.
benefits: Run your own business in Greece

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Children of Greek parent(s) acquire Greek citizenship automatically. Diaspora Greeks may claim based on grandparent ancestry.

Naturalization.desc:
**Requirements:** 7 years legal residence (3 years for EU/EEA citizens), Greek language A1 level, knowledge of Greek culture, renunciation of previous nationality.

**Processing:** Through local authorities, 6-12 months.

Spouse of Greek Citizen.desc: Spouses may apply after 1 year marriage with 3-year total residence requirement.

Historic Greek Communities.desc: Descendants of historic Greek diaspora may claim citizenship through Ministry of Interior.

tax_advice:
- Greece has progressive income tax (9% to 44%)
- Corporate tax rate is 22% (reduced rates available for certain sectors)
- VAT at 24% (reduced rates of 13%, 6%, and 0%)
- Non-residents taxed on Greece-source income only
- Golden Visa holders (€250k property purchase) receive residency without restrictions
- Capital gains taxed at 15% (under certain conditions)
- Foreign tax credits available
- Special incentive zones offer reduced corporate tax rates
local_tips:
- Greek helpful but English widely spoken in expat/tourist areas
- Bureaucracy can be slow; relationships matter; be patient
- Healthcare acceptable in major cities; private insurance recommended
- Cost of living very reasonable; budget €800-1,200/month comfortable
- Golden Visa program well-known; property investment pathway clear
- Island-specific regulations; research specific island before moving
- Summer extremely hot; adapt schedule to late nights and siestas
